case: Súmrak ('Twilight') case: charge of founding a criminal group, abuse of office and endangering tax secrecy (2022)
type: criminal investigation (Fico as accused); charge annulled before indictment
description: On 19 April 2022 an investigator of the National Criminal Agency (NAKA), in the operation code-named Súmrak supervised by the Special Prosecutor's Office (ÚŠP), charged four people identified as R. F., R. K., T. G. and N. B.: Robert Fico, then Smer-SD chairman and an opposition MP, former Interior Minister Robert Kaliňák, former Police President Tibor Gašpar and businessman Norbert Bödör. According to the ÚŠP, Fico and Kaliňák were charged with founding, conspiring and supporting a criminal group and with abuse of authority of a public official, and all four with the repeated crime of endangering commercial, banking, postal, telecommunications and tax secrecy. According to the Slovak Spectator, police suspected that confidential tax data had been extracted from the authorities and used to discredit political rivals, former President Andrej Kiska and OĽaNO leader Igor Matovič. Kaliňák was detained; because Fico was a sitting MP, taking him into custody required the consent of the National Council, which it refused on 4 May 2022. Fico rejected the accusations, linking the charge on social media to recent statements by Prime Minister Eduard Heger and the police president about action 'at the highest political levels' (noviny.sk, 20 April 2022); Kaliňák described the prosecution as politically commissioned.
outcome: On 29 November 2022 First Deputy Prosecutor General Jozef Kandera, deciding on the accused's motions on behalf of Prosecutor General Maroš Žilinka under §363 of the Criminal Procedure Code, annulled the charges against all four and the resolution opening prosecution for the criminal-group offence, citing violations of the Criminal Procedure Code and the Criminal Code (among other things, the charge did not define the period or place of the alleged conspiracy, and the tax-secrecy offence was insufficiently described), and ordered the investigator to act again. Fico said he respected the decision and had not contacted the Prosecutor General. According to the Slovak Spectator, the annulment came when the accused were already studying the case file and an indictment was about to be filed. On the ÚŠP's instruction of 18 December 2023, the investigator reopened a prosecution 'in the matter' (vo veci, against no named person) for the criminal-group offence on 2 January 2024; nobody was charged. The ÚŠP itself was abolished on 20 March 2024. No new charge against Fico has been reported in the sources consulted as of October 2026.
court: NAKA investigator supervised by the Special Prosecutor's Office; Prosecutor General's Office of the Slovak Republic (§363 decision)
presumption_note: Fico was charged but never indicted or tried, and the charge was annulled by the Prosecutor General's Office in November 2022; as of October 2026 no new charge has been reported. He is presumed innocent and rejected the accusations. The annulment was a prosecutorial decision on procedural and legal defects, not a court ruling on the facts; prosecutors of the Special Prosecutor's Office publicly criticised the Prosecutor General's use of §363 in politically exposed cases (January 2023).
key_facts: Charge brought on 19 April 2022 by a NAKA investigator in the Súmrak operation; confirmed by the police and the ÚŠP on 20 April 2022.
4 May 2022: the National Council refused consent to take MP Fico into custody (74 of 150 MPs present voted in favour; Smer-SD and the non-attached Hlas-SD MPs voted against; Sme rodina abstained).
29 November 2022: the Prosecutor General's Office annulled the charges against Fico, Kaliňák, Gašpar and Bödör under §363 of the Criminal Procedure Code.
2 January 2024: prosecution reopened 'in the matter' only, with nobody charged (Prosecutor General's Office spokeswoman Jana Tökölyová, via TASR).
Fico and Kaliňák also complained to the European Court of Human Rights and the Constitutional Court about the proceedings (see separate record).

case: Complaints by Fico and Kaliňák to the European Court of Human Rights and the Constitutional Court over the Súmrak proceedings
type: applications for the protection of fundamental rights (Fico as applicant/complainant)
description: Fico and Robert Kaliňák applied to the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) arguing that, given what they described as the general systemic bias of the Special Prosecutor's Office (ÚŠP), the supervision of the investigation against them was not impartial, and that the Prosecutor General had arbitrarily treated their objection of bias against all ÚŠP prosecutors as a request to transfer the case, depriving them of an effective remedy. They maintained the application after the charges were annulled in November 2022, arguing among other things that they had received no compensation and that the charges could be brought again. In October 2022 they also filed constitutional complaints in Slovakia objecting that a pre-trial judge of the Specialised Criminal Court had not decided their remedy himself in August 2022 but forwarded it to an ÚŠP prosecutor; according to the reporting, they sought €5,000 each in non-pecuniary damages.
outcome: Both rejected. The ECtHR declared the applications inadmissible as a whole (announced by the Slovak Ministry of Justice and reported by TASR on 27 March 2023): after the Prosecutor General's November 2022 decision no proceedings determining a criminal charge against them were pending, fair-trial guarantees of independence and impartiality apply to courts rather than prosecutors, and it was questionable whether domestic remedies had been exhausted because the objection had not been put to the Constitutional Court. The Constitutional Court rejected the constitutional complaints as manifestly unfounded by a decision of its senate (Robert Šorl, Peter Straka, Martin Vernarský) of 19 September 2024, reported in October 2024; Judge Straka dissented, arguing the case should have been admitted and a preliminary question referred to the Court of Justice of the EU.
court: European Court of Human Rights (Strasbourg); Constitutional Court of the Slovak Republic
presumption_note: In these proceedings Fico was the applicant, not an accused; their rejection says nothing about guilt or innocence. The underlying criminal charge against him was annulled in November 2022 and he remains presumed innocent.
key_facts: ECtHR inadmissibility decision reported on 27 March 2023 (via the Slovak Ministry of Justice).
Constitutional complaints filed in October 2022; rejected by a Constitutional Court senate on 19 September 2024, with a dissent by Judge Peter Straka.
By the time of the Constitutional Court decision, Fico was again Prime Minister and Kaliňák Defence Minister.

case: Charges over statements endorsing convicted far-right MP Milan Mazurek (defamation of nation, race and belief; incitement to hatred; approval of a crime)
type: criminal investigation (Fico as accused); charges annulled
description: On 5 December 2019 a NAKA investigator charged Fico, then chairman of the governing Smer-SD and an MP (not a member of the government), with defamation of nation, race and belief and incitement to national, racial and ethnic hatred, in conjunction with approval of a criminal offence. The charge concerned a video Fico posted after the Supreme Court's final conviction of ĽSNS MP Milan Mazurek for remarks about Roma; according to the police, Fico publicly agreed with statements the Supreme Court had found criminal, and according to Rádio Slovakia International he said in the video that Mazurek had said what almost the whole nation thinks. The charge followed an ÚŠP prosecutor's annulment of the investigator's earlier decision to dismiss the matter. The offences carried one to five years' imprisonment. Fico contested the charge.
outcome: Special Prosecutor Dušan Kováčik annulled the whole resolution charging Fico with effect from 31 December 2019 and ordered the investigator to act and decide again (ÚŠP spokeswoman Jana Tökölyová, via TV JOJ). In April 2021 NAKA charged Fico again on the same facts; Special Prosecutor Daniel Lipšic annulled that charge ex officio as unlawful, Prosecutor General's Office spokesman Dalibor Skladan said on 9 April 2021. No further charge has been reported.
court: NAKA investigator; Special Prosecutor's Office (Úrad špeciálnej prokuratúry)
presumption_note: Fico was never indicted or tried in this matter; both charges were annulled by the Special Prosecutor's Office, the second as unlawful. He is presumed innocent.
key_facts: First charge: 5 December 2019, under Prime Minister Peter Pellegrini (Smer-SD), who declined to comment on it.
First charge annulled by Special Prosecutor Dušan Kováčik as of 31 December 2019.
Second charge on the same facts annulled by Special Prosecutor Daniel Lipšic in April 2021.

case: Charge of incitement over the Smer-SD car-convoy protest during the COVID-19 state of emergency (December 2021)
type: criminal investigation (Fico as accused); charge annulled
description: On the evening of 16 December 2021 police took Fico, then an opposition MP, to a police station shortly before a Smer-SD protest convoy was due to start on Tyršovo nábrežie in Bratislava, at a time when public gatherings were banned under the COVID-19 state of emergency, and charged him with the offence of incitement (podnecovanie). Fico rejected the charge as invented, said its only purpose was to prevent him from taking part in the protest, and described the police action as intimidation by Interior Minister Roman Mikulec, acting Police President Štefan Hamran and Special Prosecutor Daniel Lipšic.
outcome: On 3 January 2022 the supervising prosecutor of the Bratislava Regional Prosecutor's Office upheld Fico's complaint and annulled both the charge and the resolution opening the prosecution, citing, according to spokesman Juraj Chylo, the absence of the objective and subjective elements of the offence, in part in connection with an MP's free mandate, and the inability of Fico's calls to cause mass non-compliance with a legal duty; the prosecutor also found that the way Fico's presence had been secured for the procedural acts was unlawful. The police said the matter itself was still being dealt with; no new charge against Fico has been reported.
court: Bratislava Regional Police Directorate; Bratislava Regional Prosecutor's Office (Krajská prokuratúra v Bratislave)
presumption_note: Fico was never indicted; the charge was annulled by the supervising prosecutor in January 2022. He is presumed innocent.
key_facts: Detention and charge: 16 December 2021.
Prosecutor's decision on Fico's complaint: 3 January 2022; made public by Fico on 10 January 2022 and confirmed by the police.
Hlas-SD leader Peter Pellegrini said the annulment, if confirmed, showed an attempt by the government to intimidate the opposition.

case: Criminal complaint over Fico's publication of a video of the S-300 transfer to Ukraine (2022)
type: criminal complaint against Fico (reported person); rejected by police
description: In 2022 SaS MP Ján Benčík filed a criminal complaint against Fico, then an opposition MP, on suspicion of espionage and of endangering classified, confidential and restricted information, after Fico published on social media a video of the transfer of the S-300 air-defence system to Ukraine before the transfer had been officially announced. Benčík argued that the video could have endangered the soldiers and railway workers involved. Fico called the accusations nonsensical and said the government had lied when it said it did not intend to donate the S-300 to Ukraine.
outcome: The police rejected the complaint. According to the spokeswoman of the Bratislava Regional Police Directorate, quoted by SME in April 2023, the matter was closed in June 2022 by a final resolution rejecting the case (odmietnutie veci). No prosecution was opened and Fico was not charged.
court: Police Corps, Bratislava Regional Police Directorate
presumption_note: No criminal prosecution was opened and Fico was never charged; the complaint was rejected with final effect in June 2022. He is presumed innocent.
key_facts: Complaint filed in 2022 by SaS MP Ján Benčík.
Final resolution rejecting the case: June 2022 (reported April 2023).

case: Criminal complaint by SaS leader Branislav Gröhling alleging treason and other offences over halting emergency electricity supplies to Ukraine (2026)
type: criminal complaint against Fico (reported person); police preliminary review
description: At the end of February 2026, during the dispute with Ukraine over the halt of oil transit through the Druzhba pipeline, the opposition party Freedom and Solidarity (SaS) filed criminal complaints with the Prosecutor General's Office against Prime Minister Fico over his statements and steps towards stopping emergency electricity supplies to Ukraine. According to SaS leader Branislav Gröhling, the complaints concern suspected abuse of authority of a public official, treason, inhumanity, breach of duty in the administration of another's property and a terrorist attack; he said more than 13,000 people joined the complaint. The Prosecutor General's Office passed it to the Bratislava Regional Prosecutor's Office (SME), and on 26 March 2026 Gröhling said the police had started investigating Fico.
outcome: On 27 March 2026 the Police Corps Presidium told TASR that the Office for Combating Organised Crime (ÚBOK) was reviewing the content of the complaint and assessing whether the facts described constitute a criminal offence, and gave no further details. This is a preliminary review (preverovanie), not a prosecution: no criminal proceedings against Fico have been reported and he has not been charged. No later decision was found in the sources consulted as of October 2026.
court: Police Corps Presidium – Office for Combating Organised Crime (ÚBOK); Bratislava Regional Prosecutor's Office
presumption_note: Fico has not been charged and no prosecution against him has been reported; the complaint reflects allegations by a political opponent that no authority has found substantiated. He is presumed innocent.
key_facts: Complaints filed with the Prosecutor General's Office at the end of February 2026.
Passed to the Bratislava Regional Prosecutor's Office, then examined by ÚBOK.
Police statement of 27 March 2026: review of whether the facts constitute a crime under way; no details given.

case: Assassination attempt in Handlová, 15 May 2024: trial of Juraj Cintula (Fico as injured party)
type: criminal trial (Fico as injured party, poškodený)
description: On 15 May 2024, after an off-site government meeting in Handlová, Juraj Cintula, then 71, from Levice, fired five shots at Prime Minister Fico with a legally held firearm as Fico approached supporters, seriously injuring him. Cintula was detained at the scene and remanded in custody by the Specialised Criminal Court on 18 May 2024. He was first charged with attempted premeditated murder; in July 2024 the charge was requalified as a terrorist attack. The prosecutor filed the indictment for the particularly serious crime of a terrorist attack against a protected person on 17 March 2025, and the trial opened on 8 July 2025 at the Specialised Criminal Court's Banská Bystrica branch. Fico did not attend; he was represented by his lawyer and adviser David Lindtner, who said Fico, as the injured party, had forgiven the defendant. Cintula admitted the shooting but said he wanted to stop Fico from performing the office of Prime Minister, not to kill him, and disputed the terrorism qualification. According to SME, Fico repeatedly said during the investigation that Cintula was connected to opposition parties; this was not shown, and the trial did not examine any such link.
outcome: On 21 October 2025 the Specialised Criminal Court (presiding judge Igor Králik) found Cintula guilty of a terrorist attack and sentenced him to 21 years' imprisonment, applying extraordinary mitigation (the offence otherwise carries life imprisonment) because of his age, clean record and health; the prosecutor waived her right to appeal and Cintula appealed. On 29 April 2026 the Supreme Court dismissed his appeal, slightly corrected the description of the act and its legal qualification, and upheld the guilty verdict for a terrorist attack and the 21-year sentence; the judgment is final and cannot be appealed. The case is closed.
court: Specialised Criminal Court (Špecializovaný trestný súd), Banská Bystrica branch; appeal: Supreme Court of the Slovak Republic (Najvyšší súd SR)
presumption_note: Fico was the victim (injured party) in this case, not an accused. The defendant, Juraj Cintula, was convicted with final effect by the Supreme Court on 29 April 2026. No court has found that anyone else, including any political party, was involved in the attack.
key_facts: Attack: 15 May 2024, Handlová, five shots fired.
Charge requalified from attempted premeditated murder to terrorist attack in July 2024; indictment 17 March 2025; trial opened 8 July 2025.
First-instance verdict: 21 October 2025, 21 years for a terrorist attack (not final).
Supreme Court: appeal dismissed on 29 April 2026; verdict and sentence final.
Fico was represented by David Lindtner, who welcomed the first-instance verdict and qualification.

case: Fico v. Slovakia (European Court of Human Rights): covert surveillance of meetings at a hunting lodge
type: application to the European Court of Human Rights (Fico as applicant)
description: Fico complained before Slovak courts about the covert recording, while he was in opposition, of his meetings with lawyers of detained persons at a hunting lodge in southern Slovakia; the recordings leaked to the media in 2021 and Fico called them illegal and contrary to democracy. He also challenged the way the police had obtained court approval for monitoring the lodge, including camera recordings, which according to the reporting had been justified by suspected poaching. He sought €33,000 in compensation and was unsuccessful before the Constitutional Court. On 25 May 2023 he applied to the ECtHR, alleging violations of his rights to a fair trial and to respect for private and family life.
outcome: On 6 November 2023 the ECtHR communicated the case to the Slovak government and asked it to respond, in particular on whether Fico had a fair hearing in the Constitutional Court proceedings and whether the use of surveillance means was lawful, necessary and limited to its stated purposes. Since October 2023 the respondent government has been led by Fico himself, as SME noted. No decision or judgment had been reported in the sources consulted as of October 2026.
court: European Court of Human Rights (Strasbourg); earlier: Constitutional Court of the Slovak Republic
presumption_note: Fico is the applicant; the case concerns alleged violations of his rights by the state, not any accusation against him.
key_facts: Application lodged on 25 May 2023; communicated to the government on 6 November 2023 (confirmed by the ECtHR, reported by ČTK on 27 November 2023).
Domestic claim for €33,000 in compensation failed at the Constitutional Court.
Registered as Fico v. Slovakia.

case: President Zuzana Čaputová v. Robert Fico: personality-rights lawsuit (2023)
type: civil lawsuit for protection of personality (Fico as defendant)
description: On 13 September 2023, two weeks before the early parliamentary election, President Zuzana Čaputová filed a lawsuit for protection of personality against Fico, then leader of the opposition Smer-SD. According to her spokesman Martin Strižinec, the reason was 'gross lies and fabricated accusations' that Fico kept spreading about her, including unfounded accusations of violating the constitution and laws or serving a foreign power; she said the lawsuit protected primarily the institution of the presidency. According to Denník N, Fico and other Smer politicians had repeatedly called her an 'American agent'. Fico said the head of state was suing the strongest opposition politician two weeks before the election and was thereby interfering in the campaign.
outcome: No ruling, settlement or withdrawal has been reported in the sources consulted as of October 2026; the outcome could not be confirmed.
court: Slovak civil court of first instance (the court was not named in the reports consulted)
presumption_note: Fico is the defendant in a civil case; no court has ruled that his statements infringed Čaputová's personality rights. The case concerns civil liability only, not any criminal accusation.
key_facts: Lawsuit filed on 13 September 2023, after Čaputová announced in May 2023 that she would take legal action.
Čaputová had earlier won a similar case against Smer MP Ľuboš Blaha, according to Denník N.
Čaputová's term as President ended in June 2024.

case: Fico v. Peter Bárdy and Ringier Slovakia Media: lawsuit over his photograph on the cover of the book 'Fico – Posadnutý mocou' (2024–2026)
type: civil lawsuit for protection of personality (Fico as plaintiff)
description: In autumn 2024 Prime Minister Fico sued Peter Bárdy, editor-in-chief of Aktuality.sk and author of the book 'Fico – Posadnutý mocou' (Fico – Obsessed with Power), and the publisher Ringier Slovakia Media, arguing that he had never consented to the use of his likeness on the book's cover; he sought €100,000 in non-pecuniary damages from each. His lawyer David Lindtner argued the cover served commercial purposes not covered by an artistic or news licence. Ringier described the suit as a SLAPP (a lawsuit aimed at intimidating the media), which Lindtner rejected.
outcome: At the hearing on 2 June 2026, which Fico did not attend, his lawyer withdrew the claim against Bárdy because Bárdy had not designed the cover. The judge of the Municipal Court Bratislava IV dismissed the claim against Ringier, finding that Fico's rights had not been infringed: the photograph was taken while he was performing his public function, the publisher held a licence to use it and the book, including its cover, qualifies as a work; she also called the amount claimed excessive. The judgment was not final at the time; Bárdy said he expected an appeal. No appeal ruling has been reported as of October 2026.
court: Municipal Court Bratislava IV (Mestský súd Bratislava IV)
presumption_note: Fico is the plaintiff in a civil case; the defendants are not accused of any crime. The first-instance judgment dismissing his claim was not final at the time of reporting.
key_facts: Lawsuit filed in autumn 2024; €100,000 claimed from each defendant (€200,000 in total).
2 June 2026: claim against Bárdy withdrawn; claim against Ringier Slovakia Media dismissed at first instance.
Fico was represented by David Lindtner (Kallan Legal), also his adviser.

case: Fico v. Petit Press (publisher of SME): lawsuit over a 2009 cartoon by Martin 'Shooty' Šútovec
type: civil lawsuit for protection of personality (Fico as plaintiff)
description: In 2009, while Prime Minister, Fico sued Petit Press, publisher of the daily SME, over a cartoon by Martin Šútovec ('Shooty') published on 9 July 2009 that showed him at a doctor's appointment with an X-ray reading 'no spine'; Fico argued that it mocked him, while the cartoonist said 'no backbone' was a figure of speech about character. He sought an apology and €33,000 (one million Slovak crowns) in non-pecuniary damages.
outcome: On 13 July 2010 the Bratislava IV District Court rejected the lawsuit, and Fico's lawyer said they would appeal. According to the Slovak Spectator, the regional court also rejected it; Fico then filed an extraordinary appeal with the Supreme Court, which returned the case to the regional court over a procedural fault (a document had not been delivered to Fico). In March 2013 Fico, again Prime Minister, decided to withdraw the lawsuit; his spokesman Erik Tomáš confirmed to SME that Fico had instructed his lawyer to end the case.
court: District Court Bratislava IV (Okresný súd Bratislava IV); Regional Court in Bratislava; Supreme Court of the Slovak Republic
presumption_note: Civil case; the defendant publisher was not accused of any crime. Fico's claim was rejected at first instance and later withdrawn, so no court found that his rights had been infringed.
key_facts: Cartoon published on 9 July 2009; claim of €33,000 plus an apology.
First-instance rejection: 13 July 2010; the regional court also rejected the claim.
Supreme Court returned the case to the regional court on procedural grounds; Fico withdrew the lawsuit in March 2013.

case: Fico v. publisher of the weekly Plus 7 Dní: lawsuit over an article about his meeting with Muammar Gaddafi
type: civil lawsuit for protection of personality (Fico as plaintiff)
description: Fico sued the publisher of the weekly Plus 7 Dní, demanding an apology and about €33,000 in damages, over an article in which editor-in-chief Miloš Luknár expressed ironic opinions about Fico's meeting with Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi. According to the weekly's deputy editor-in-chief Radovan Kyška, cited by SITA, the content of the talk was not made public and Fico said only after journalists insisted that he had spoken with Gaddafi about a fight against global imperialism; Fico argued in the lawsuit that this was not true.
outcome: Fico lost. A district court dismissed the lawsuit in March 2009 and the Regional Court in Bratislava upheld that ruling; its decision was delivered to the publisher on 10 November 2010 and could not be appealed.
court: District court in Bratislava; appeal: Regional Court in Bratislava (Krajský súd v Bratislave)
presumption_note: Civil case; the publisher was not accused of any crime. The courts dismissed Fico's claim with final effect.
key_facts: First-instance dismissal: March 2009.
Appeal ruling delivered 10 November 2010; final.

case: Ivan Mikloš v. Robert Fico: lawsuit over accusations of kickbacks in the privatisation of the gas utility SPP
type: civil lawsuit for protection of personality (Fico as defendant)
description: Finance Minister Ivan Mikloš (SDKÚ) sued Fico, then leader of the opposition Smer, over statements accusing him of receiving kickbacks in the privatisation of the national gas utility SPP. At a Smer press conference in February 2003 Fico had also hinted that Mikloš might be wealthier than former Prime Minister Vladimír Mečiar. Fico, a lawyer, represented himself and stood by his statements, saying the privatisation contract was disadvantageous and that 'if people sign disadvantageous contracts, usually they get something in return'.
outcome: In a ruling reported in March 2004 the district court ordered Fico to publish an apology in several specified media but rejected Mikloš's claim for Sk600,000 (about €14,851) in compensation and his argument that the statements had damaged his political support. Fico criticised the court for ruling in his absence without notifying him of the date of the main hearing and said he was considering an appeal to the Regional Court. The outcome of any appeal could not be confirmed in the sources consulted.
court: District court (first instance; its seat is not stated in the report consulted)
presumption_note: Civil case concerning statements; no criminal accusation was involved. The first-instance ruling went against Fico on the apology; whether it became final could not be confirmed.
key_facts: Statements made in 2003 about the SPP privatisation.
First-instance ruling reported on 8 March 2004: apology ordered, no damages awarded.

case: Libel charge against Igor Matovič over his claim that Fico held a secret account in Belize (Fico as injured party)
type: criminal investigation of another person (Fico as the allegedly defamed person and a witness)
description: Police charged opposition leader Igor Matovič (OĽaNO-NOVA) with libel after he accused Prime Minister Fico of having a secret account and a shell company in Belize; according to the prosecutor, Matovič had not presented his own opinion but information from an anonymous letter. Fico, the person allegedly defamed, gave testimony in the case.
outcome: On 14 December 2016 the charge against Matovič was dropped. According to Matovič's lawyer Daniel Lipšic, quoted by TASR, the prosecutor found the prosecution unjustified, considered the investigator's questions to the Prime Minister leading, and found that testimonies recorded in almost identical wording could not serve to confirm guilt. Richard Vašečka, head of the OĽaNO-NOVA caucus, said the Prime Minister had used the case to threaten the opposition.
presumption_note: Fico was the injured party, not an accused. The libel charge against Igor Matovič was dropped, and Matovič was presumed innocent; no court ruled on the claims about the alleged account.
key_facts: Matovič's claim concerned an alleged secret account and shell company in Belize.
Charge dropped on 14 December 2016 after the prosecutor reviewed the case.
